published_prior_art.cite: MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local leaves directional differentiability without centrosymmetry for future work; Yata2025Optimal solves the centrosymmetric Gaussian benchmark via a modulus extremizer.

ZhangWuLopez2010Exchange supplies the compact semi-infinite exchange template; AradillasFernandezEtAl2025Epsilon certifies a fixed finite menu rather than an unrestricted Gaussian Bayes-envelope game.
MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision proves multiplicity and rules out linear thresholds under additional conditions, but does not give this asymmetric triangular coexistence construction.

MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local gives the centrosymmetric directionally differentiable solver; the stated strict overlap inclusion is mainly a comparison corollary once the triangular witness is established.

MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision establishes multiplicity and qualified threshold exclusions, while Yata2025Optimal gives an optimal selected index under centrosymmetry; neither gives a primitive necessary-and-sufficient classification of the full correspondence.

Tetenov2012Asymmetric derives exact asymmetric-regret solutions in point-identified normal, Bernoulli, and bounded-outcome experiments, not a partially identified Gaussian-mixture saddle with a certified curved boundary.
MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local provides feasible selected-rule transfer, but the proposed extension obtains feasibility only after assuming stronger two-sided total-variation and joint-TV premises.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem tie-uniform-lan-transfer
novelty_flags.one_line: The feasible clause is only an o(1) bound conditional on un-derived two-sided experiment equivalence and joint-TV approximation, with no verified named model delivering those premises, rate, strict bound improvement, or first-result comparison.

soundness_flags.label: def:stable-selector; Theorem tie-uniform-lan-transfer
soundness_flags.one_line: The tolerances are merely nonnegative, so epsilon_n or epsilon_nu may equal zero although the exchange construction only guarantees asymptotic gap convergence and need not terminate at zero; require strictly positive tolerances or specify an exact-solver branch.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem tie-uniform-lan-transfer, primitive-game stability clause
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The explicit modulus is conditional on the compact kappa-bounded primitive-game collection and does not cover unbounded domains, covariances, or face coefficients.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Uniform value and certified-selector stability only on the stated kappa-bounded polyhedral Gaussian game class.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:estimated-game-legality and ass:estimated-game-kappa-bounds
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Feasible selection is conditional on an estimated game that is legally constrained into the game class and numerical envelope almost surely.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The selector guarantee applies only to constrained estimators satisfying legal membership and the kappa bounds; those conditions are not consequences of coefficient bounds alone.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section “Solving the Limit Problem,” Assumption 5, Theorems 4–5, and Conclusion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper separately solves fully differentiable non-centrosymmetric and directionally differentiable centrosymmetric cases, and its Conclusion identifies dropping centrosymmetry with directional differentiability as an open extension.
Theorem 1 assumes a convex centrosymmetric parameter space and gives a minimax-regret rule under normal errors within the class of all decision rules.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv v3, 20 Jun 2025; published ReStud version not publicly inspectable in this review
source_verification_receipts.locator: Definition “Nontrivial partial identification” and Theorem 3 in the main text
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited preprint defines sign ambiguity on an open set, proves infinitely many MMR rules under additional conditions, and gives qualified exclusions of linear threshold rules rather than a full-correspondence classification.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv version accessed; EC 2025 proceedings page was access-restricted
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies epsilon-minimax optimization where the statistician randomizes among I fixed decision rules, using a Hedge/mirror-subgradient method over the finite simplex.
The paper derives exact finite-sample asymmetric-minimax-regret solutions for normal, Bernoulli, and bounded-outcome experiments.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace nonnegative certificate tolerances by epsilon_n, epsilon_nu > 0, or add a separately specified exact-saddle branch when a tolerance equals zero.

Instantiate the two-sided Le Cam and joint-TV premises in one named original experiment, deriving them from primitive sampling and nuisance conditions; otherwise remove feasible transfer from the headline and retain it as a conditional corollary.

State a comparison theorem against the feasible rule of MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local on the exact overlap and quantify a strict asymmetric-polyhedral advantage beyond the definitional overlap inclusion.

recommended_next_step: Revise the selector’s zero-tolerance gap and either derive the transfer premises in a named model or narrow the transfer result to an explicitly conditional secondary corollary before advancing.
